title: Probabilistic demotion policy for tier routing with SLA hedging and quota-aware prioritization
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Goal: Implement a probabilistic demotion admission controller for tier-based routing that (1) respects per-tenant and per-plan quotas, (2) hedges SLAs for enterprise customers by reserving capacity, and (3) applies soft, probabilistic demotions for free and paid tiers instead of abrupt hard rejections.

Motivation: Current tier routing uses deterministic demotions and strict spillbacks which cause noisy failures and poor UX for bursty free-tier workloads. We want a smoother degradation curve that preserves enterprise SLAs, reduces tail latency spikes, and improves fairness across tenants during capacity pressure.

Design summary:
- Admission model: compute an admission probability p in [0,1] per request based on: remaining quota fraction (EWMA over consumption rate), recent latency headroom, and plan priority multiplier.
- SLA hedging: keep a soft-capacity reservoir (configurable percentage of total fastpath) reserved for enterprise plans. The admission controller reduces p for lower tiers first but never drops enterprise below a minimum floor except under emergency.
- Probabilistic demotion semantics: instead of immediate fallback to cheaper model or rejection, a request with probability 1-p will be routed to: (a) a slightly higher-latency batch lane for same model variant if available, or (b) a lower-cost quantized model variant with deterministic quality labels. The policy prefers routing to batch lanes before model variant fallback.
- Quota-aware prioritization: tenants with remaining quota fraction < threshold enter a penalty-softening curve where p decays progressively; tenants with recent high error rates or abusive behavior have an accelerated decay (penalty box multiplier).
- Predictive credit budgeting: EWMA-based consumption forecast for each tenant to anticipate imminent quota exhaustion and pre-emptively adjust p to avoid cascaded failures.
- Regional awareness: admission decisions respect region affinity. If local capacity is constrained, the controller will consider cross-region spill (following policy) but will prefer degraded local variants before cross-region routing to avoid added latency.
- Observability: expose per-tenant admission p, reason codes, quota fraction, predicted exhaustion ETA, and routing decision in trace spans and the Console dashboard.

Success criteria (metrics):
- Decrease free-tier request rejection rate by >= 40% under 5x baseline burst tests while keeping enterprise p95 latency within SLA (no more than 10% degradation).
- Reduce severity-incident rollbacks caused by hard demotions by 90% in canary.
- Fairness index improvement (Jain's index) across non-enterprise tenants during sustained load.

Rollout plan:
- Feature flag gated; default off.
- Stage 1: Simulation run in playback mode against 7 days of production traces to tune EWMA windows and p mapping (owners: Ravi + Sarah).
- Stage 2: Canary enablement for a small fraction of free/paid traffic in a single region (eu-west-1); monitor latency, error rate, admission histograms, and fairness metrics.
- Stage 3: Gradual ramp with traffic-split experiments (A/B) and canary to 10% global, then 50%, then 100% if metrics stable.
- Rollback: immediate feature-flag off and fallback to current deterministic router. Runbook entry created for multi-region spill anomalies.
